
## Sinusoid Equation

The objective of this section is to define the mathematical signal that will be generated in Python. We first describe a 1 Hz sinusoidal signal with an amplitude of 1 and no phase shift. This provides the reference signal for the x-axis before introducing phase shifts for the y- and z-axes.

A sinusoidal signal can be described by:
$$s(t) = A \sin(2\pi f t + \phi)$$

where:

- $A$ is the amplitude,
- $f$ is the frequency in Hz,
- $t$ is time in seconds,
- $\phi$ is the phase shift in radians.

For this signal:
$$A = 1, \qquad f = 1 \text{ Hz}, \qquad \phi = 0$$

Therefore, the sinusoid along the x-axis is:

$$x(t) = \sin(2\pi t)$$

A frequency of 1 Hz means that the signal completes one full cycle every second. Therefore, over 3 seconds, the signal completes three cycles.
